Coal collision core 3.0.4
Upstream: https://github.com/coal-library/coal/releases/tag/v3.0.4
Archive SHA256: 0A4F58E55B88A3D9F873CE79979AECC08491D212EA0B9311DF013DF3B22BFFAC
Eigen 3.4.0: https://gitlab.com/libeigen/eigen/-/releases/3.4.0
Archive SHA256: 8586084F71F9BDE545EE7FA6D00288B264A2B7AC3607B974E54D13E7162C1C72
Boost headers 1.87.0: https://archives.boost.io/release/1.87.0/source/
Archive SHA256: F55C340AA49763B1925CCF02B2E83F35FDCF634C9D5164A2ACB87540173C741D

Build: powershell -File src/third_party/coal/prepare-coal.ps1 -Configuration Debug
Use Release for the release CRT. No debug/release STL boundary is mixed.
Downloaded upstream files are unmodified. CMake generates a build-local copy
of Minkowski dispatch with a neighbor-topology guard: point-only convex hulls
use the exact linear support scan, including hulls larger than 32 vertices.
CMakeLists.txt builds a static
collision core, omitting model loaders, archives, Octomap and Python. Generated
configuration headers in config/ select this feature set. iCAX provides model
IO and persistence, so Assimp and compiled Boost libraries are not needed.
This core is linked only into CoalCollisionServices.dll. Public framework
interfaces contain no Coal, Eigen, Boost or OpenCascade types.
Each configuration installs dependency license notices; both development
staging and the FiveAxisCAM package copy those notices with the program.

The CAD consumer prepares a dedicated trimmed collision mesh with OCCT surface
deflection control (0.05 mm). Coal stores it in native OBBRSS triangle BVHs,
shared between per-face and complete-obstacle models. The larger of requested
and reported mesh deflection, plus CAD face/edge/vertex tolerances, is included
as a security margin. This is a tolerance-controlled collision representation,
not a claim of mathematically exact tessellation. It is independent of display
mesh quality. Unresolved mesh bounds continue to the exact CAD kernel.
If meshing is unavailable, positive-weight spline pole hulls or conservative
boxes are used. Coal evaluates point support maxima directly; Qhull is not
needed. Head frusta conservatively enclose circular cross sections. Overlap or
solver non-convergence cannot certify clearance. Continuous motion bounds,
solid containment, cancellation and model revision invalidation remain in the
geometry/CAM layers that already own them. No machine-level NC qualification
is implied by a head-envelope clearance result.
